His shoulders slump, not in relief but in resignation. “I’ll cease the memory‑sweeping,” he declares, the word sounding like a promise and a threat in the same breath. The guards behind him tighten their grips on their scrolls, eyes darting toward the iron fence that surrounds his tower. Mitch, the man whose face still bears the faint crimson of the bloodstains, follows a shadowy figure—Serah, the healer whose reputation for restorative magic is whispered in hushed awe. Her hands are steady as she places a bandage over the wound that had once bled from his forehead. “It’ll heal,” she murmurs, her voice a soft counterpoint to the clamor of the square. Around them, traders pause mid‑trade, guards tighten their patrols, and the townsfolk murmur. The lanterns flicker, throwing long shadows across the cobbles. Even the street performer Jorin, who had been playing a mournful tune, lowers his lute, the music stuttering into silence. The night feels heavy, as though the town itself is holding its breath, waiting to see if the fragile truce will hold or if the tide will rise again.
